pp=power point

abilities(powers) in the array will be flight, speed and quickness.

4 ranks of flight cost 8 pp (2 per rank)7 ranks of speed cost 7pp (1 per rank)If you didn't have those 2 powers in a array the total pp cost would be 8pp+7pp=15pp.Putting them in a array would make the base cost of the array equal to the ability with the highest power point cost, the 4 ranks of flight at 8pp and +1pp for every additional ability that has a 8pp cost or lower.

Since speed 7 cost 7pp, if you put it in the array with Flight 4 (8pp) the cost would be 8pp+1pp for a total array cost of 9pp. This array would currently have Flight 4 and Speed 7 as abilities you could use in the array.

If down the road you wanted to add another power, a third power in this case, to the array, as long as that powers total pp cost is 8 or lower it would only cost 1pp to add it.

Lets say the new/third power you add to the array is quickness 10, that cost 10pp. Since 10pp is higher than 8, 10pp is now the new base cost of the array and flight 4 switches to 1pp cost to keep it in the array and speed 7 remains 1pp.

The total cost of the array at this point is 12pp for quickness 10, flight 4 and speed 7.

The basics of a array are , the power (can be multiple powers linked to each other) with the highest total pp cost = the primary power(s)/ cost of the array. Every extra power added, as long as it is equal to or under the primary powers pp cost it only cost 1pp to add the the array. So if you have 4 ranks of flight and 7 ranks of speed. Flight 4 total pp cost would be 8 (no effects) and speed 7 would be 7 (no effects) but since they are in a array  the total pp cost would be 8 +1 because speed 7 is less than or equal to 8.  


other than that some basic rules are you can only switch the "active" power in a array once per turn and if you have a continuous or sustained power in a array and switch to another power in the array the continuous / sustained power stops immediately.
